topic: Namespaces and Scope Resolution with Classes and Visibility
explanation: Namespaces in C++ are used to organize code into logical groups and prevent name collisions. The scope resolution operator (::) allows access to names within specific namespaces or classes, enabling precise control over name visibility and linkage. Understanding how scopes are searched and resolved is essential for managing large codebases, especially when dealing with nested namespaces, classes, and inheritance hierarchies.
